title: Spicy Coated Groundnuts
author: Fran Osseo-Asare
desc: A pound of raw peanuts in a spiced batter fried at around 360 degrees — the browner they are, the crispier, but not past burnt.
longDesc: Coated groundnuts are sold in bags all over Ghana and this is the documented version: eight ounces of flour with three teaspoons of ground cayenne, a teaspoon of salt, a quarter teaspoon of white pepper and a teaspoon of baking powder, bound with a quarter cup of evaporated milk, about four tablespoons of water and two eggs, coating a pound of shelled raw unsalted peanuts with their skins on. The oil goes to around 360 degrees. Her doneness cue is a judgement rather than a point: the browner they are, the crispier they'll be, but being careful they do not cross the line to burned.
ingredients: 1 lb shelled raw unsalted peanuts with skins — about 3 cups Spanish peanuts
3 tsp ground dried red cayenne pepper
1/4 cup evaporated milk, plus about 4 tbsp water
steps: Combine the flour, cayenne, salt, white pepper and baking powder.
Beat the evaporated milk, water and eggs together.
Mix the wet into the dry to make a thick batter.
Stir in the raw peanuts with their skins on, so each is coated.
Heat the oil to around 360 degrees Fahrenheit.
Fry in batches, separating the clusters.
The browner they are, the crispier they will be — but be careful they do not cross the line to burned.
Drain and cool completely before storing.
chefTips: Her cue is a judgement and it is honest: the browner they are, the crispier they will be, but do not let them cross the line to burned. There is no fixed point.
Raw peanuts, not roasted. They cook in the batter, and pre-roasted nuts will be overdone by the time the coating crisps.
Skins on. They add colour, a little bitterness and most of the antioxidants.
Three hundred and sixty degrees is on the hot side for a battered item, which is what gets the coating crisp before the nut overcooks.
A thick batter, not a thin one. Four tablespoons of water is the adjustment — add it gradually.
Cool completely before storing or the steam will soften the coating.
Spanish peanuts are specified as the three-cup equivalent. They are small, round and skin-on, which is exactly what this wants.
commonMistakes: A thin batter, which slides off.
Frying too cool, so the coating absorbs oil.
sources: Adapted from 'Recipe #69: Spicy coated groundnuts', betumiblog.blogspot.com, 30 June 2011. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Posted by Fran'. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).

Ingredients exactly as printed: 8 oz flour (1 1/2 to 2 cups unsifted); 3 teaspoons ground dried red cayenne pepper; 1 teaspoon salt; 1/4 teaspoon white pepper; 1 teaspoon baking powder; 1/4 cup evaporated milk (plus about 4 tablespoons water); 2 eggs; 1 pound shelled raw unsalted peanuts with skins (about 3 cups Spanish peanuts); oil to around 360°F.
THE DONENESS CUE, quoted from the first fetch, and it is a judgement rather than a point: 'The browner they are, the crispier they'll be, but being careful they do not cross the line to burned.'
NOTE THE FLOUR RANGE: '8 oz flour (1 1/2 to 2 cups unsifted)'. Eight ounces as a weight is firm; the cup equivalent spans a third more at the top end, which tells you to trust the weight.
NO YIELD is printed. The ten servings above is an editorial division of a pound of peanuts plus batter.
THE PEANUTS ARE RAW, which is the key difference from kuli-kuli (GHA072), where roasted peanuts are ground and pressed. Here the nut cooks inside its coating.
NO SPECIFIC FRYING TIME is printed — only the temperature and the browning judgement. That absence is recorded.

This is one of a cluster of peanut preparations documented in this collection: kuli-kuli as de-oiled pressed cakes (GHA072), tankora as the powder made from them (GHA064), dzowoe as uncooked spiced peanut balls (GHA092), and this as a battered fried snack. Four quite different things from one nut.
storage: 2 weeks in an airtight tin once completely cool.
reheating: A low oven briefly to re-crisp.
healthBenefits: Peanuts supply protein, niacin, folate, magnesium and vitamin E.
The skins carry most of the nut's antioxidant polyphenols.
Eggs and evaporated milk add complete protein.
Capsaicin from three teaspoons of cayenne.
culturalNote: Coated groundnuts are sold in twisted paper and plastic bags at every Ghanaian lorry park and junction, and they are the snack that goes with a bottle of something cold. The batter is what makes them Ghanaian rather than merely roasted nuts — spiced, crisp and faintly sweet from the milk.
